I am a little confused on how I can fix this error that I am getting for the GGIR Outputs for Parts 2,3,4 and 5.

Basically, I am running GGIR on a lot of raw gt3x files (I have also run it on some .bin files from a different project - where I did not face this issue. So it may be that there is an issue with the read_gt3x function, or with my files. I do not have these files in any other format other than the raw gt3x.)

I have attached the output from the raw Gt3x files (the first night's sleep onset and wakeup time seems to be duplicated across all the nights for the same participant - this is a very common theme across all participants - I am looking at about a hundred participants, several nights per participant). In the day summary outputs, there is another (slightly smaller) concern that GGIR assumes the sleep onset to be at 10 PM and wakeup to be at 7 AM on many days (maybe due to insufficient data), although the duplication of sleep onset and wakeup time has been significantly reduced. I wonder if there is a better approach for this as well.

Hi Mayank,

I see that all the nights with SPT defined from 22 to 7 have a cleaningcode = 5, meaning that either you defined to relyonguider on those nights in your data_cleaning_file, or that GGIR did not find any sustained inactivity bout overlaping with the guider window in those nights. More information here: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter10_SleepAnalysis.html#quality-assurance:~:text=follow%20scenario%202.-,Quality%20assurance,-Cleaningcode

Also, it it difficult to tell what guider was used and how it behaved from your screenshots. The guider column is missing in most of them. I see it is available in the first screenshot, but the guider for those nights state "nosleeplog", and I have never seen this definition of guider in GGIR. Did you modify this column?

When SPT is not identified, the last backup approach in GGIR is to define SPT from 21 to 7 (not 22 to 7), and this is very weird to occur, and in such a case, you would receive a warning. See here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/g.part4.R (lines 279:284).

It may be easier if you can identify one specific file for which this is occurring and if you are able to investigate what the data look like in those nights with the SPT defined from 22 to 7.

Best,
Jairo

Hi Jairo,

Thank you for your response.

I had a feeling that relyonguider should not be TRUE so I did set it to FALSE actually when I did this analysis again (which is what you see in the results actually). I did read about the cleaning code as well, and was very confused about that.

In our study there was no sleep diary that participants used, and the guider GGIR used is mostly HDCZA and sometimes L512. In the day summary - out of 5,250 days 897 nights have the variable "nosleeplog_accnotworn". To answer your question about the nosleeplog, I did not modify it (unless there is a variable from the GGIR code/config.csv file). I wonder if this is mostly because GGIR did not detect reliable sleeping patterns. 

However, I can see that regardless there are some nights where the first night's sleep onset time is repeated over the next few nights for some reason, which is the main issue I want to try to resolve to get more reliable data.

I was also wondering, if you have used the read_gt3x function as well in the past, you find the GGIR outputs from it reliable usually?

Thank you,

May

On Thursday, October 10, 2024 at 3:27:42 AM UTC-3 Jairo Hidalgo Migueles wrote:
Hi Mayank,

I see that all the nights with SPT defined from 22 to 7 have a cleaningcode = 5, meaning that either you defined to relyonguider on those nights in your data_cleaning_file, or that GGIR did not find any sustained inactivity bout overlaping with the guider window in those nights. More information here: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter10_SleepAnalysis.html#quality-assurance:~:text=follow%20scenario%202.-,Quality%20assurance,-Cleaningcode

Also, it it difficult to tell what guider was used and how it behaved from your screenshots. The guider column is missing in most of them. I see it is available in the first screenshot, but the guider for those nights state "nosleeplog", and I have never seen this definition of guider in GGIR. Did you modify this column?

When SPT is not identified, the last backup approach in GGIR is to define SPT from 21 to 7 (not 22 to 7), and this is very weird to occur, and in such a case, you would receive a warning. See here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/g.part4.R (lines 279:284).

It may be easier if you can identify one specific file for which this is occurring and if you are able to investigate what the data look like in those nights with the SPT defined from 22 to 7.

Best,
Jairo
